facts: Q2 2026 revenue was $508 million versus $506 million in Q2 2025, while system shipments increased 3% year over year.
EyeQ/SuperVision average system price declined to $48.5 in Q2 2026 from $49.7 in Q2 2025, attributed mainly to higher China OEM mix.
Six-month operating cash flow was $210 million and property/equipment purchases were $51 million; Mobileye reported $1.4 billion of cash, marketable securities and deposits.
Updated FY2026 revenue guidance is $1.970-$2.020 billion, implying 4%-7% year-over-year growth.

Updated adjusted operating income guidance is $365-$425 million, but the improvement is primarily attributable to the Israeli R&D incentive law; Q2 included about $93 million non-GAAP incentive offset covering the first half.

A high-volume Cloud-Enhanced ADAS design win with Stellantis was added; Mobileye states gross profit per unit is roughly equivalent to Surround ADAS and more than double current average base-ADAS profitability.

MOIA public user testing in Hamburg with safety drivers remained on track, while Mobileye was engaging vendors for vehicle supply, self-driving-system installation/upfit and fleet logistics for vertically integrated robotaxi operations.

factors.name: financialOperatingMomentum
factors.basis: Cash generation and raised revenue outlook are positive, but quarterly revenue was essentially flat and reported operating improvement is materially incentive-supported.

factors.name: pricingPower
factors.basis: Average system price fell year over year as China OEM mix increased.

factors.name: catalystScore
factors.basis: Stellantis Cloud-Enhanced ADAS win plus late-2026/2027 advanced launches and robotaxi testing provide identifiable commercial milestones.

factors.name: bottleneckControl
factors.basis: Integrated EyeQ/ADAS stack and higher-value advanced programs support control, while robotaxi vertical integration adds dependence on vehicle, upfit and fleet-logistics vendors.

factors.name: supplyChainResilience
factors.basis: Primary source confirms vendor engagement for robotaxi vehicle/upfit/logistics but does not establish redundancy or concentration sufficient for a stronger conclusion.

risks: Do not treat the raised adjusted operating-income outlook as purely organic operating leverage; management attributes most of the revision to the R&D incentive law.
Lower ASP from China OEM mix is a direct pricing/mix pressure signal.
Vertically integrated robotaxi operations introduce execution, fleet and vendor dependencies beyond the historical supplier model.
contradictions: Headline operating-margin improvement can appear stronger than underlying operations because the first-half R&D incentive was recognized in Q2; Alpha should normalize this when constructing numeric underwriting.
unknowns: Current market valuation inputs were not established by this primary-source acquisition.
The source does not quantify probability/timing of converting the broader advanced-product pipeline into recognized revenue beyond stated guidance and milestones.
Supply-chain redundancy and vendor concentration for the vertically integrated robotaxi model remain unquantified.
authorityBoundary: Source acquisition only. No numeric Earth Score, underwriting score, causal disposition, rank, tick or Chief decision is asserted.
